# 5.2 Fenwick tree (BIT), inversion counting

Phase 5 (Range data structures), target rating 1800–2100. Bank status: short.

## Patterns

### Point updates, prefix sums (`point-prefix`)

Change single elements and query prefix or range sums, both in O(log n).

**Works because:** The operation is invertible (sum), so a range sum is a difference of two prefix sums.

### Counting inversions (`inversions`)

Count pairs i < j with a[i] > a[j] by inserting values left to right and asking how many larger ones are present.

**Works because:** Values (after compression) index the tree, and pairs are counted from the later element's side.

### Range updates, point reads (`range-add-point`)

Add to a range and read single elements, using the tree over a difference array.

**Works because:** A point's value is the prefix sum of the difference array.

### Offline counting by sorting (`offline-sorted-count`)

Answer counting queries ("distinct values in [l, r]", points in rectangles) by sorting queries and updates together and sweeping.

**Works because:** All queries are known in advance, so processing order can be chosen to make each query a prefix query.

### k-th present element (`kth-in-tree`)

Find the k-th smallest present value by descending the tree bit by bit.

**Works because:** Counts are non-negative, so prefix counts are monotone and the descent can choose each bit greedily.
